sections.heading: Naitik Pareshbhai Mawani vs State Of Gujarat on 1 September, 2025
content: 1. Rule returnable forthwith. Learned APP waives service of notice of rule for respondent - State of Gujarat.

2. By way of the present application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short "BNSS"), the applicant has prayed for anticipatory bail in the event of arrest in connection with the FIR being C.R. No.I-11218019250002 of 2025 registered with Cyber Crime Police Station, Porbandar for the alleged offences as mentioned in the FIR.

3. The sum and substance of the case of the prosecution is that the accused No.1, in collusion with the other co-accused whose names are there in the FIR as well as those who will be found during the course of investigation, hatched a criminal conspiracy, and thereby, committed the alleged fraud, which is said to have been uncovered during the investigation of a different crime, wherein the police have gathered information regarding some suspicious bank accounts being used in committing Cyber crimes, wherein the details of 14 bank accounts of Kotak Mahindra Bank at M.G. Road, Porbandar were also received, and upon preliminary investigation being carried Page 1 of 18 Uploaded by ABDULVAHID A SHAIKH(HC00955) on Sat Sep 06 2025 Downloaded on : Mon Sep 08 21:46:42 IST 2025 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined out of those 14 bank accounts regarding whether there is any Cyber complaint being registered relating to the said accounts, it was found that out of the aforesaid 14 accounts, various complaints of cheating and fraudulent transactions have been registered in the different States in relation to 05 accounts, and upon further inquiry being made, it was found that the address mentioned in the said 05 accounts is the very same, which belongs to the accused No.1-Hiralba Bhurabhai Jadeja, and as such, search proceedings was carried out at the residential premises of the accused No.1, wherefrom various bank accounts details were found by the investigating officer, and upon further inquiry being made and statements of various persons being recorded, it was found that all those bank accounts got opened at the instance of the accused No.1 in the names of her associates, which was alleged to have been used in an online defrauding and duping the gullible people of the different States by luring and tempting them of giving profit upon investment being made and of securing a job for them as also by representing them as the Telecom Regulatory Authority, and thereby duped number of gullible people of different States of Lakhs of rupees. With this sort of allegations, the present FIR has been registered.

4. Thus, apprehending his arrest pursuant to the registration of the aforesaid FIR, the applicant preferred anticipatory bail before the trial court, however, the trial court has not entertained the said application and rejected the same.
5. Being aggrieved, the applicant is here before this Court with the present application.

6. Learned advocate Mr. Ekant Ahuja for learned advocate Ms. Shivani J. Lad appearing for the applicant submits that the allegations made in the FIR are of such a nature, for which, Page 2 of 18 Uploaded by ABDULVAHID A SHAIKH(HC00955) on Sat Sep 06 2025 Downloaded on : Mon Sep 08 21:46:42 IST 2025 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined custodial interrogation of the applicant at this stage is not necessary. He further submits that the applicant will keep himself available during the course of investigation as well as the trial proceedings and will not flee from justice. He further submits that total six persons have been arraigned as accused in the FIR, however, the present applicant has not been named in the FIR, but subsequently, during the course of investigation, on the basis of the statement made by the co-accused, he has been falsely dragged into the present offence, and is seriously apprehending his arrest at the hands of the investigating officer. Learned advocate Mr. Ahuja further submits that the FIR came to be lodged on 14.05.2025 for the offence alleged to have taken place on 29.05.2024, and as such, there is a gross delay of almost one year in registering the FIR without there being any plausible explanation worth the name about such delay in registering the FIR. Learned advocate Mr. Ahuja also submits that looking to the FIR, all the allegations are against the accused No.1, at whose instance, the alleged bank accounts were opened, in the names of purportedly bogus companies, and for the KYC whereof, documents of naive and gullible people were utilized. Learned advocate Mr. Ahuja further submits that in the case on hand, some of the account holders have been shown as the witnesses and some have been shown as the accused, which clearly shows that the concerned investigating officer had adopted a pick and choose policy. He also submits that whatever allegations are there in the FIR, are all against the accused No.1 and her associates, and the present applicant is not directly or indirectly connected with the commission of offence, and he has been falsely dragged into the offence. It was the accused No.1, who played a pivotal role in perpetuating the alleged fraud inasmuch Page 3 of 18 Uploaded by ABDULVAHID A SHAIKH(HC00955) on Sat Sep 06 2025 Downloaded on : Mon Sep 08 21:46:42 IST 2025 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined as she solicited assistance of the accused No.2 and one Ajay Chauhan, who procured the KYC documents of several persons for the purposes of incorporating allegedly bogus companies and opening their bank accounts in lieu of monetary payment to the tune of INR 20,000/-.

7. Learned advocate Mr. Ahuja further submits that pursuant to the registration of the FIR, the investigation was commenced, and at the end of it, charge-sheet also came to be submitted against the co-accused, and along with the charge-sheet, statements of the persons in whose names accounts were opened, were placed, however, the statements of the victims are not forming the part of the charge-sheet papers. Learned advocate Mr. Ahuja submits that, in fact, the present applicant has not received any monetary gain out of the alleged transactions, which is clearly apparent from the charge-sheet papers submitted by the investigating officer qua the other co- accused. He submits that the implication of the present applicant is being made on the ground that he had provided certain guidance in the opening of the bank accounts, and as such, one cannot be made an accused solely on the ground that he has provided certain assistance in opening the bank accounts. Moreover, mere de-freezing of account also does not make out any case against the applicant. He further submits that, in fact, after coming to know about his name being given as the co- accused, the present applicant preferred an application under Section 343 of the BNSS, 2023 and Section 344 of the BNS, 2023, seeking tender of pardon and to be turned as an approver by voluntarily disclosing all the true facts germane to the offence in question that are within his knowledge, however, the said application came to be rejected by the trial court solely on the Page 4 of 18 Uploaded by ABDULVAHID A SHAIKH(HC00955) on Sat Sep 06 2025 Downloaded on : Mon Sep 08 21:46:42 IST 2025 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined ground that the applicant did not remain present personally. Thus, in the light of the aforesaid application filed by the applicant, wherein he has given a full and true disclosure of the facts and circumstances engulfing the subject FIR with the intent to aid the investigating officer to unearth the truth, the necessity to arrest the applicant stands dissipated as the applicant has disclosed everything in his knowledge and established his bona fide while doing so in the said application. He further submits that the protection of personal liberty is a rule and curtailment thereof is an exception. The applicant is ready and willing to render full cooperation in the investigation as has been doing by him throughout. He submits that no recovery or discovery remains from the applicant in view of full and true disclosure made by him in the application, seeking tender of pardon. Moreover, the alleged offences are triable by the Court of Magistrate. To buttress his aforesaid submissions, learned advocate Mr. Ahuja has placed reliance upon the decision in the case of P. Krishna Mohan Reddy vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, Special Leave Petition (Criminal) No.7532 of 2025, decided on 16.05.2025.

8. In such circumstances, referred to above, learned advocate for the applicant prays that there being merit in the present application, the same be allowed and the applicant be released on anticipatory bail.

9. On the other hand, the present application has been vehemently opposed by the learned APP Ms. Jyoti Bhatt. Learned APP Ms. Bhatt submits that the present applicant has committed a very serious offence in connivance with the other co-accused. She submits that it is the specific case of the prosecution that all the accused persons, in connivance with each other, hatched a conspiracy, and as a part of the said conspiracy, Page 5 of 18 Uploaded by ABDULVAHID A SHAIKH(HC00955) on Sat Sep 06 2025 Downloaded on : Mon Sep 08 21:46:42 IST 2025 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined played their individual roles, wherein the accused No.1 has played a vital role. She further submits that the entire scam was unearthed by the police while investigating into altogether a difference offence, during which period, the concerned investigation officer gathered information about some accounts being used in committing cyber crimes, wherein some accounts were found, which got opened by the accused No.1 in the names of her associates. Therefore, the police had carried out intensive investigation, upon which, the involvement of the present applicant has also been found out. Learned APP Ms. Bhatt submits that based upon the same set of documents, certain account have also been opened in Junagadh City, and number of gullible people have also been duped at Junagadh also by the said accused persons, for which, a separate FIR has also been filed at Junagadh. She further submits that, in fact, during the course of investigation, it is found out that an amount of Rs.79,92,088/- has been fraudulently obtained and then withdrawn by the co-accused person from the said accounts. Learned APP Ms. Bhatt also submits that the arrested co-accused persons have very categorically stated in their statements that all the current/saving bank accounts, that have been opened at Porbandar, Junagadh, Jamnagar and Rajkot, were got opened under the guidance of the present applicant, and after even after opening it, the same were being managed by the present applicant. Moreover, the statements of number of witnesses have also been recorded by the investigating officer, wherein they have also categorically mentioned the name of the present applicant along with his specific role.

10. Learned APP Ms. Bhatt further submits that even after the alleged accounts got freezed, the present applicant went to the Page 6 of 18 Uploaded by ABDULVAHID A SHAIKH(HC00955) on Sat Sep 06 2025 Downloaded on : Mon Sep 08 21:46:42 IST 2025 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined Bank along with the other co-accused to defreeze the account and supplied certain documents, which is clearly evident from the CCTV footages of the Bank collected by the investigating officer. She submits that during the course of investigation, the investigating officer has recorded statements of number of persons including the witnesses as well as the Bank Officers, from which, the name as well as specific role of the present applicant has clearly come on surface, which indicates that the present applicant has actively participated in the commission of the offence. She submits that, in fact, in all it is a huge scam of Rs. 163 Crores. Moreover, the concerned investigating officer has also inquired from the NCCRP/Samanvay portal that whether any other offence is registered against the 26 current accounts run by the accused persons, upon which, it was found that in all 123 complaints of cyber fraud have been registered against the 19 accounts in various States, and there are all possible chances that the said number is likely to be increased during the course of investigation. She submits that, in fact, there are in all ten FIRs have been registered against the present applicant at the different police stations within the State of Gujarat. Moreover, during the period when the offence was committed, the present applicant was in constant touch along with the other co-accused, which is evident from the CDR collected by the investigating officer. Even the conversation took place between present applicant and the accused No.1 on WhatsApp has also collected by the investigating officer, which shows that the present applicant is directly involved in the commission of the crime. Not only that, the accused No.1 also sent money to the present applicant through Angadiya firm, which is also evident from the statement of the person of the Angadiya firm recorded by the Page 7 of 18 Uploaded by ABDULVAHID A SHAIKH(HC00955) on Sat Sep 06 2025 Downloaded on : Mon Sep 08 21:46:42 IST 2025 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined investigating officer. Thus, the cumulative effect of the materials collected by the investigating officer so far, suggests that the present applicant is closely associated with the other co-accused and has played an active role in the commission of the crime, and has also received a huge amount as a commission from the accused No.1 through Angadiya firm. The applicant himself has also sent certain amount to the accused No.1 through Angadiya firm, and those materials have also been collected by the investigating officer. Learned APP Ms. Bhatt further submits that if the application made by the present applicant to become an approver is to be read, then it appears that in the said applicant itself, the present applicant has narrated how he has acted in a particular manner at the time of committing the crime. She submits that moreover, the present applicant is a resident of Mumbai, and is evading his arrest since inception, and if he is released on anticipatory bail, there is a likelihood of he being fled away from the Country as he is holding a passport as also the IP addresses of the Bank Accounts of the co-accused and the witnesses got opened by the present applicant are found to be of foreign countries. Thus, it is apparent on the face of the record that all the accused persons, in connivance with each other, have committed the offence. It is submitted that the applicant has failed to establish case for extraordinary relief.
11. In such circumstances, referred to above, learned APP Ms. Bhatt prays that there being no merit in the present application, the same be rejected.
12. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the record.

13. It is well settled that, among other circumstances, the Page 8 of 18 Uploaded by ABDULVAHID A SHAIKH(HC00955) on Sat Sep 06 2025 Downloaded on : Mon Sep 08 21:46:42 IST 2025 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined factors to be borne in mind while considering an application for bail are (i) whether there is any prima facie or reasonable ground to believe that the accused had committed the offence;

(ii) nature and gravity of the accusation; (iii) severity of the punishment in the event of conviction; (iv) danger of the accused absconding or fleeing, if released on bail; (v) character, behaviour, means, position and standing of the accused. Though at the stage of granting bail execution and appreciation of evidence is not permissible. Hence, custodial interrogation is required.

14. It appears from the record that there is a huge scam of crores of rupees alleged to have been committed by the present applicant along with the other co-accused by opening various bank accounts in the name of the other co-accused and the witnesses, which were then being used in committing the cyber fraud with the gullible people. From the record, it reveals that the amount involved in the said scam is Rs.163 Crores. The record reveals that very serious allegations of fraud and siphoning away of huge amount of gullible people have been made against the present applicant and the co- accused. The allegations seems to be quite serious in nature. Moreover, from the materials placed on record, prima facie, the involvement of the present applicant is also found out. There are number of statements of the witnesses as well as the co-accused, wherein they have very categorically stated the name of the present applicant along with his specific role. Even from the CDR (Call Data Records) collected by the investigating officer, it clearly appears that the present applicant was in constant touch along with the other co-

NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined accused as well as the witnesses during the period when the offence was committed. Further, there are in all total ten FIRs have been registered against the present applicant alleging similar kind of offence, which indicates that the applicant seems to be an habitual offender in committing such kind of offences. That apart, there are certain transactions took place between the applicant and the accused No.1 through Angadiya firm, which is also evident from the statement of the person of the Angadiya firm recorded by the investigating officer. Not only that, from the statement of the Bank Officer as well as one of the witnesses, it appears that the present applicant personally went to the Bank along with the other co-accused along with certain documents for the purpose of defreezing the alleged accounts, which is also evident from the CCTV footages of the Bank. Thus, from the materials collected and produced before this Court, I am of the view that prima facie involvement of the present applicant is clearly found out in the commission of the crime. It also appears that number of cyber complaints have been registered in the different States as well as within the State of Gujarat against the accounts got opened by the present applicant in the name of the co-accused and the witnesses. Further, the offence with which the applicant is charged with is an economic offence and is against the interest of the society.

15. It goes without saying that the alleged offence of misappropriating crores of rupees of the gullible people is quite grave in nature. Hence, while it is extremely important to protect the personal liberty of a person, it is equally incumbent upon me to analyze the seriousness of the offence and Page 10 of 18 Uploaded by ABDULVAHID A SHAIKH(HC00955) on Sat Sep 06 2025 Downloaded on : Mon Sep 08 21:46:42 IST 2025 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined determine if there is a need for custodial interrogation.

16. In Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra , (2011) 1 SCC 694, the Supreme Court carefully considered the principles established by the Constitution Bench in Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab , (1980) 2 SCC 565. After a thorough deliberation, the Supreme Court arrived at the following conclusion:

23. Coming to the case on hand, from the allegations levelled in the FIR and the materials placed on record, it appears that the very serious allegations of siphoning away of of crores of rupees have been made against the applicant. Moreover, the present case also falls within the category of economic offences and the amount involved in the present case is quite huge, and it is trite law that in economic offences, benefit of pre-arrest bail should not be extended in favour of the accused in a casual manner. Thus, at this stage, in my view, custodial interrogation of the applicant is very much necessary.

24. Lastly, it may be noted that as held in catena of decisions, the economic offences constitute a class apart and need to be visited with a different approach in the matter of bail. The economic offences having deep-rooted conspiracies and involving huge loss of public funds need to be viewed Page 15 of 18 Uploaded by ABDULVAHID A SHAIKH(HC00955) on Sat Sep 06 2025 Downloaded on : Mon Sep 08 21:46:42 IST 2025 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined seriously and considered as grave offences affecting the economy of the country as a whole and thereby posing serious threat to the financial health of the country. Undoubtedly, economic offences have serious repercussions on the development of the country as a whole. To cite a few judgments in this regard are Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy vs. Central Bureau of Investigation , reported in ( 2013) 7 SCC 439, Nimmagadda Prasad vs. Central Bureau of Investigation , ( 2013) 7 SCC 466, Gautam Kundu vs. Directorate of Enforcement (Prevention of Money- Laundering Act), Government of India Through Manoj Kumar, Assistant Director, Eastern Region , ( 2015) 16 SCC 1, State of Bihar and Another vs. Amit Kumar alias Bachcha Rai, (2017) 13 SCC 751. The Supreme Court taking a serious note with regard to the economic offences had observed as back as in 1987 in case of State of Gujarat vs. Mohanlal Jitamalji Porwal and Another , (1987) 2 SCC 364 as under:-
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined

25. Moreover, when the Court is satisfied that a prima facie case of custodial interrogation of the accused is made out by the prosecution for securing the incriminating materials from the information likely to be received from the accused, then the power under Section 482 should not be exercised in a routine manner. The presence of the applicant, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, seems to be needed to uncover the truth. Further, the discretion under Section 482 cannot be exercised with regard to offences punishable with death or imprisonment for life, unless the court at that very stage is satisfied that such a charge appears to be false or groundless. The larger interest of the public and State demand that in serious cases like economic offences involving cheating and misappropriation of huge volume of amount, the discretion under Section 482 of the BNSS should not be exercised.

26. Thus, what is discernible from the above is that while deciding anticipatory bail application, it is the first duty of the Court to see seriousness of the offence, prima facie case and interest of the society at a large. Therefore, when no special and compelling circumstances are made out and no case of false implication of present applicants in the alleged offence is made out before this Court, I am of the opinion that this Court should refrain itself from exercising its discretionary powers in favour of the present applicant at this stage.

27. Further, the present applicant is involved in white collar socio-economic offence which constitute a class apart and needs to be visited with a different approach. The economic Page 17 of 18 Uploaded by ABDULVAHID A SHAIKH(HC00955) on Sat Sep 06 2025 Downloaded on : Mon Sep 08 21:46:42 IST 2025 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/15696/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/09/2025 undefined offences adversely affect the economic and social fabric of the country. In such circumstances also, grant of anticipatory bail at this stage would frustrate the investigation.

28. In view of above discussion and considering the materials produced before this Court, I am of the opinion that there seems to be a prima facie involvement of the present applicant in the commission of the alleged offence. Thus, this Court is of the opinion that at the initial stage of the investigation of the offence, grant of anticipatory bail in favour of the applicant is likely to hamper the investigation and investigating agency is likely to lose an opportunity to exploit all the fact situation, probabilities or opportunities which the Agency may get during the custodial interrogation of a person, and therefore, keeping in mind all the factors, no interference is required at this stage. The impugned order passed by the trial court, rejecting anticipatory bail application of the applicant is just and proper and does not require any interference at the end of this Court.

29. In the result, the present application, being devoid of any merit, is hereby rejected. However, it is made clear that the observations made by this Court herein above at this stage while deciding the anticipatory bail application, would not come in the way of the applicant at the time as and when if ultimately the trial court is proceeded with the trial, and at the stage of consideration of regular bail application, if preferred by the applicant. Rule is discharged.
(DIVYESH A. JOSHI,J) VAHID Page 18 of 18 Uploaded by ABDULVAHID A SHAIKH(HC00955) on Sat Sep 06 2025 Downloaded on : Mon Sep 08 21:46:42 IST 2025
